incidents.vector: Compromised GitHub maintainer account used to push a self-propagating credential-stealing worm (Mini Shai-Hulud / 'Miasma' variant) into Red Hat's package pipeline.
incidents.impact: 32 packages downloaded ~117,000 times per week were tainted with credential-stealing malware; Red Hat removed the affected packages and says no customer action is currently required, though knock-on supply chain risk to downstream developers remains.

incidents.victim: Obama White House & U.S. Space Force Instagram accounts (Meta)
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers tricked Meta's AI customer-support bot into linking a new email to target accounts during a password reset workflow, then completed account takeover without needing the original credentials.
incidents.impact: Both accounts were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian images and messaging; Meta pushed an emergency patch and says no back-end database was breached, but a number of high-value short Instagram handles were also stolen for resale.

incidents.vector: Smart-contract bug in the bridge that moves assets between Ethereum and Cosmos was exploited to drain funds.
incidents.impact: $5.4 million in crypto assets drained from the bridge; trading was halted over the weekend pending investigation.

incidents.vector: Researcher-demonstrated exploit against the service prompted PostHog to rotate all AWS credentials.
incidents.impact: Service outage as PostHog rotated all AWS credentials; the company says no customer data was compromised.

incidents.vector: Credential-stuffing attack against 23andMe customer accounts (original 2023 breach now subject to a California AG lawsuit alleging the company failed to defend against a common attack type).
incidents.impact: Personal and genetic information of nearly 7 million Americans exposed in the underlying 2023 breach; California Attorney General Rob Bonta has now sued the company for inadequate protections.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated cloud server left exposed to the internet without a password for at least a week.
incidents.impact: More than 3.4 million scanned images of driver's licenses, legal documents and financial records belonging to inmates and their contacts were exposed before the server was secured.

incidents.vector: Legacy protocols in an older DeFi launchpad service were exploited to drain old liquidity pools.
incidents.impact: $7.3 million in crypto stolen from legacy DxSale liquidity pools.

incidents.vector: Not yet publicly detailed; ShinyHunters extortion group listed Charter on its dark-web leak portal, prompting the company to confirm a breach.
incidents.impact: Charter has confirmed a security breach; scope of stolen data not yet disclosed.

incidents.victim: FBI Director Kash Patel's 'Based Apparel' merchandise store
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised the storefront and injected ClickFix social-engineering pages.
incidents.impact: Visitors to the store were served ClickFix lure pages designed to deliver malware via fake browser prompts.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; the Play ransomware group claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from the corporate network.
incidents.impact: Play group claims theft of sensitive corporate financial documents and is extorting the company; MyPillow has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Attackers used compromised credentials issued to other Lithuanian government agencies that had authorized access to the land and real-estate registry.
incidents.impact: 600,000 records stolen, including real names, cadastral information and other property-specific details.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; intrusions reportedly went initially undetected.
incidents.impact: Two unnamed agencies whose networks store the personal data of millions of Vietnamese citizens were breached; investigation is ongoing.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands
incidents.vector: Not disclosed; officials did not confirm whether the incident is ransomware.
incidents.impact: Email servers across the US territory's government were disrupted, slowing administrative operations.

incidents.victim: Russian Social Design Agency (SDA) disinformation operation
incidents.vector: Not publicly described; intruders obtained internal SDA documents and shared them with selected journalists.
incidents.impact: Internal documents detailing Russian disinformation operations targeting Armenia, France, Ukraine, Germany, Moldova and Norway were leaked, including identities of foreign collaborators (a retired US General, a former Bundestag member and others).

incidents.attacker: Unknown — actively exploited in the wild
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-9082, an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in Drupal Core.
incidents.impact: CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, ordering federal agencies to remediate; thousands of Drupal-based public-facing sites are exposed pending patching.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million patients had medical data stolen, including irreplaceable biometric information such as fingerprints and palm prints, which affected individuals cannot replace.

incidents.vector: Malicious VS Code 'Nx Console' extension (compromised in the upstream TanStack supply-chain attack) was installed on a GitHub employee device, giving attackers access to internal repos.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800–4,000 internal GitHub source-code repositories were exfiltrated; the criminal group demanded $50,000 for the stolen code and threatened to leak it for free if no buyer came forward. GitHub is rotating critical secret tokens.

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with administrative access intentionally created a public GitHub repo ('Private-CISA') containing plaintext credentials, disabling GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protections.
incidents.impact: AWS GovCloud keys and dozens of internal credentials (including an RSA key with full access to the CISA-IT GitHub organization) were exposed publicly since at least November 2025; lawmakers including Sen. Hassan and Rep. Thompson have demanded answers, and CISA is still working to invalidate keys more than a week after notification.

incidents.vector: Same TanStack supply-chain compromise that hit GitHub; malicious package distributed via a compromised JavaScript dependency.
incidents.impact: Grafana confirmed it was breached and traced the intrusion to the TanStack supply-chain attack; scope of impact still being assessed.

incidents.victim: Russia-linked hosting infrastructure (MIRhosting / WorkTitans / 'the[.]hosting') — Dutch takedown
incidents.vector: Dutch FIOD financial-crimes investigators arrested the operators and raided three businesses and two datacenters used by Russia to stage cyberattacks, influence operations and disinformation campaigns inside the EU.
incidents.impact: More than 800 servers seized; a 57-year-old from Amsterdam and a 39-year-old Russian native were arrested for EU sanctions violations; the infrastructure had previously been used in pro-Russian DDoS and disinformation operations against Danish government bodies during the November 2025 municipal elections.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply chain credential theft
incidents.vector: Over 5,700 malicious commits injected into GitHub Actions workflows in target repositories, designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens and other secrets at build time.
incidents.impact: More than 5,500 repositories infected with malicious workflows that exfiltrate secrets; GitHub has rolled out npm Staged Publishing and invalidated previous granular access tokens to limit propagation of similar worms.

incidents.victim: Australian independent MP Zali Steggall and three staffers
incidents.vector: WhatsApp account takeover, believed to be part of a Russian campaign targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: MP Steggall and three of her staffers had their WhatsApp accounts breached by a suspected foreign state actor; details of compromised communications not disclosed.
